headings.title: SMTO-SKL-0074 — Your large file upload to OneDrive or SharePoint stopped partway

html:
SMTO-SKL-0074 — Your large file upload to OneDrive or SharePoint stopped partway

GUID: 30c3ae6d-1f69-562c-b219-93ad31b49a22
Slug: microsoft365-file-upload-failed
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • SMTO was sending a large file to OneDrive or SharePoint in pieces, and the transfer got out of step and stopped before the last piece. The file is most likely not there yet, but check before trying again.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open OneDrive or the SharePoint library in your browser with the same Microsoft account and look for the file in the folder you chose. The upload usually stops before the file is created, but checking first avoids a duplicate.
  2. If the file isn't there, ask SMTO to upload it again to the same folder and approve the upload when asked. SMTO can't pick up a stopped upload where it left off; it has to start a new one.
  3. If it fails again, make sure the file you attached in the conversation still opens, or attach it again. SMTO checks the file before sending, and a changed or damaged file can break the transfer.

What success looks like

  • The file appears once in the OneDrive or SharePoint folder with the full size you expect.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the file name and size, to the person who manages SMTO's Microsoft 365 setup. Don't start several uploads of the same file at once.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Microsoft 365 upload session failed before completion: a source chunk read came back empty before the expected size, Graph's nextExpectedRanges did not match the acknowledged offset, or the upload loop ended without a completed item.

What this means

  • Upload encounters an empty source chunk before expected completion, inconsistent nextExpectedRanges, or exits without a completed result. This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Upload encounters an empty source chunk before expected completion, inconsistent nextExpectedRanges, or exits without a completed result.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect confirmed offsets, source size and current upload session before sending more bytes.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the destination folder with microsoft365.file_list or file_info under the same account_ref; an unfinished upload session does not create the item. Confirm the source artifact is intact, then start one new file_upload (upload sessions are not resumable across calls or restarts); use conflict=replace with an observed etag only if a file with that name now exists and should be overwritten.
  • Inspect source integrity and acknowledged upload offsets; reconcile the exact destination before starting another upload.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • Exact destination state is reconciled and only deliberate remaining work proceeds.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
